title: Progressive rollout gates: canary, percentage ramps, feature-flag integration, and auto-rollback
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: We need a standardized, production-safe progressive delivery system for model/runtime upgrades across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Current rollouts are manual and inconsistent: ad-hoc canaries by env, manual traffic shifting, and no unified auto-rollback criteria. This ticket defines the implementation plan for rollout gates (canaries, % traffic ramps), feature-flag integration to scope exposure, and automated rollback on defined health regressions.

Objectives:
- Provide a declarative rollout policy that engineers can attach to any model or runtime release.
- Integrate with feature-flag service (FF) so that we can do user-scoped canaries and kill-switching.
- Implement automated rollback triggers based on SLO/health signals (5xx%, latency p95, inference errors, QA eval regressions).
- Surface rollout state and rollback events in Redwood Console and in API responses for auditability.
- Ensure policies work consistently across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC) with fallback behavior when metrics are unavailable.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Core rollout controller service (k8s + fleet-aware) accepting declarative policies.
- Traffic ramp engine implementing percentage-based shifts and time windows.
- Canary selection strategies: random users, specific customer ids (via FF), header-based sampling.
- Safe-guarding: automated rollback, manual pause, and forced promote endpoints.
- Console UI additions: rollout timeline, live traffic split, abort/promote buttons, and recent metric deltas.
- Integration tests and a canary runbook + runit script.

Out of scope for this ticket:
- Per-customer billing impact estimation (follow-up).
- Deep model evaluation suites (we will call existing Eval infra).
acceptance_criteria:
- Declarative policy format accepted by rollout-controller v1.0.
- Canary flow can be executed end-to-end in staging: start at 1% for 10m, ramp to 10% over 1h, then 50% over next 4h, reaching 100% by promotion.
- Auto-rollback triggers defined and exercised: >1.25x baseline 5xx rate OR >1.5x baseline p95 latency OR explicit QA regression alert => rollback to previous stable variant within 2 minutes.
- Console displays rollout progress, and operator actions are logged to audit logs.
- Feature-flag scoping works: we can target a set of user ids via FF and revoke in <30s.
- Integration tests simulating metric regressions cause automatic rollback in CI environment.
implementation_notes:
High-level plan:
1) Schema & API: define JSON/YAML rollout policy (see example below) and create REST endpoints in rollout-controller.
2) Metrics plumbing: connect rollout-controller to observability (Prometheus metrics for Hosted, StatsD bridge for Dedicated, Push-based for Private). Define baseline_window and comparison_window.
3) Ramp engine: time-based + event hooks (on-pause, on-error). Implement graceful draining of in-flight KV caches when switching variants.
4) FF integration: use existing FF SDK to bind rollout groups to flags; add kill-switch that sets traffic to 0%.
5) Console: add rollout page + action buttons; wire audit log entries to central logging (SIEM).
6) Tests: chaos tests for partial network partitions and metric delays; e2e tests to validate rollback.

Implementation trade-offs & decisions so far:
- We choose percentage-based ramps over node-level routing to preserve model-caching locality. That may incur cross-node cache misses during early ramps but keeps logic simpler.
- Auto-rollback relies on relative deltas from baseline instead of absolute thresholds to account for model/seq-length variance.
- For Private deployments where metrics may be delayed/offline, default to manual approval unless customer opts into local metrics forwarding.

Engineering tasks (rough):
- rollout-controller service: 5 pts
- metrics adapters & detector: 3 pts
- ramp engine & gate state machine: 3 pts
- FF integration & API: 2 pts
- Console UI & audit logging: 3 pts
- e2e & chaos tests: 2 pts

Edge cases noted:
- Blue/green with kv-cache incompatibility: when promoting new variant we need to warm KV cache ahead of routing 100% traffic; plan to pre-warm using synthetic prefills for top N prefixes.
- Partial rollback when only a subset of customers shows regressions: support surgical rollback by FF group.

Security: rollout-owner action authorization will be enforced via RBAC; security review required before GA.
rollout_policy_example:
# Example policy (YAML encoded as string)
name: runtime-2.4-canary-2026-02
strategy:
  type: percentage_ramp
  stages:
    - name: canary-1pct
      duration: 10m
      target_percent: 1
    - name: ramp-to-10
      duration: 1h
      target_percent: 10
    - name: ramp-to-50
      duration: 4h
      target_percent: 50
    - name: promote
      duration: 1h
      target_percent: 100
scopes:
  - type: feature_flag
    flag_key: rollout_runtime_2_4_testers
    mode: include
health_checks:
  - name: error_rate
    metric: request_5xx_ratio
    comparator: relative_greater_than
    threshold: 1.25
    baseline_window: 1h
    comparison_window: 5m
  - name: latency_p95
    metric: inference_latency_p95_ms
    comparator: relative_greater_than
    threshold: 1.5
    baseline_window: 1h
    comparison_window: 5m
actions:
  on_failure: rollback
  on_manual_pause: hold
